extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to the journal Archives (clinical researchers, clinicians, and trial investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting manuscripts to Archives, including required reporting checklists/flow diagrams, ethical approvals, trial registration expectations, and patient privacy/consent rules. Focused on clinical research reports, case reports, systematic reviews, diagnostic studies, and randomized trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of industry-recognized reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Archives strongly encourages authors to use industry-recognized reporting guidelines such as PRISMA, STARD, and STROBE, when appropriate, to clarify that minimum reporting requirements have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click here for links to the reporting guidelines, and for further information, visit www.equator-network.org. Use the appropriate guideline for the study type to demonstrate minimum reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomized Controlled Trials: CONSORT checklist and flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: Archives requires authors to submit the CONSORT flow diagram when submitting manuscripts reporting randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide CONSORT checklist and flowchart. Links: http://www.consort-statement.org/consort-statement/overview0/ (checklist) and http://www.consort-statement.org/consort-statement/overview0/ (flowchart - required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic reviews: PRISMA checklist and flowchart
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic Reviews should follow PRISMA reporting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the PRISMA checklist and flow diagram. Link: http://www.prisma-statement.org/statement.htm (checklist and flowchart).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analyses of controlled trials: PRISMA
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-analyses of controlled trials should follow PRISMA reporting guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide PRISMA checklist and flowchart as appropriate. Link: http://www.prisma-statement.org/statement.htm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational epidemiology studies: STROBE checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational epidemiology studies should follow STROBE reporting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic accuracy studies: STARD checklist and flowchart
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic accuracy studies should follow STARD reporting guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide STARD checklist and flowchart. Link: http://www.stard-statement.org/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial registration policy (current and prospective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Archives' editors have adopted in principle the spirit of the ICMJE requirement to register prospective clinical trials at or prior to subject enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At this time registration is not a submission requirement for studies meeting ICMJE criteria, nor is full compliance with the Minimal Registration Data Set required; however, this may become mandatory in the future by prior notice. Authors who have registered their trials should provide the trial registration number in the cover letter; registration numbers will appear in all published content.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB and Animal Care Committee approval and ethical compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must certify that their institution or the appropriate regional institution approved the protocol for any investigation involving humans or animals (or that the research complied with the Declaration of Helsinki) and that the conduct of all investigation conformed to the protocol and the ethical and humane principles of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting work to Archives, include certification of ethical approval/compliance. Ensure all human- and animal-subject research follows accepted ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case reports and single-case studies: anonymity or written patient consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submitting case reports (Clinical Notes) or single-case studies (Articles) are required to assure the anonymity of patients (including names, uniquely identifying personal descriptors, detailed family trees, and geographic location) or obtain from each patient a written consent to publish the manuscript and photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subjects are not identifiable in the manuscript and photographs OR obtain written consent to publish manuscript and photographs. If patient consent is obtained, state this in the cover letter. All manuscripts must comply at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patients' rights to privacy and informed consent for identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: Patients and research subjects have a right to privacy that should not be infringed without informed consent. Identifying information will not be published in written descriptions, photographs, and pedigrees unless essential for scientific explanation and the patient (or legal proxy) gives written informed consent for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informed consent for publication requires that the patient or proxy be shown the manuscript to be published. Omit identifying details if not essential, but do not alter or falsify patient data to attain anonymity. Complete anonymity is difficult to achieve—obtain consent when doubt exists. Note: masking the eye region in photographs is inadequate protection of anonymity.
